policy.published: review-confirmed flags only, on unchanged evidence
policy.four_eyes: a flag that names a supplier needs two different reviewers to confirm it

disclaimer: Flags are automated indicators that a pattern in official data deserves a closer look. A confirmed flag means reviewers checked that the data pattern is real - not that anyone acted unlawfully.

detectors.D1_overspend_vs_budget: Spent much more than the approved budget (audited spending compared with the budget).
detectors.D3_restricted_supplier_awarded: A tender award went to a name on National Treasury's restricted-supplier list while the restriction applied.
detectors.D4_supplier_concentration: One supplier won most of a buyer's tender value over three years.
detectors.D5_award_value_gaps: Many of a buyer's published tender awards have no value, or an obviously wrong value such as R0.
detectors.D8_irregular_expenditure_trend: Reported irregular expenditure rose sharply two years in a row.
detectors.D13_fuel_unit_price: A payment for fuel works out at a much higher price per litre than the official fuel price at the time (reviewed internally; not published).
detectors.D6_threshold_splitting: Several awards by one buyer to one supplier close together, each below the competitive-bidding limit but together above it. Never published.
detectors.D16_repeat_awards: One buyer gave the same supplier many awards within a year. Never published.
detectors.D17_just_below_threshold: Repeated awards by one buyer to one supplier just under the competitive-bidding limit. Never published.
